findings.description: The EC2 user_data script exports literal AWS access key ID and secret access key values (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). user_data is stored in the Terraform state and is retrievable via the instance metadata service by anyone who can reach the instance, so these long-lived static AWS credentials are disclosed and must be rotated and replaced with an instance role.

The security group allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-forcing or exploitation of SSH. This is compounded because the same instance carries hard-coded AWS keys in its user data.

The instance has no root_block_device block, so its root EBS volume is created with the AMI/default settings and no encrypted = true; the instance's primary disk contents are stored unencrypted at rest.

The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true, so data written to the attached disk is stored in cleartext on the underlying media, and any snapshot taken from it inherits that unencrypted state.

The snapshot is taken from the unencrypted volume and has no encrypted attribute, so the disk contents are persisted as an unencrypted snapshot artifact that can be shared or restored by anyone with access to it.
The S3 bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so the network traffic metadata it archives is stored unencrypted at rest.

The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block (and no ACL/ownership controls), so it relies solely on account-level defaults to prevent public exposure of the flow-log archive; explicit blocking of public ACLs and policies is the expected secure default for a bucket holding audit data.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and every retained flow-log object to be deleted without confirmation, so the audit trail can be destroyed as part of the same action that removes the infrastructure.

The egress rule permits all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving the instance unrestricted outbound connectivity and providing no containment for data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet, including the portal server, is automatically assigned a public IP and becomes directly addressable from the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched into this subnet are automatically given public IP addresses and exposed to the internet without an explicit decision to do so.

The security group allows HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. For a public web server this is expected, but combined with the default unencrypted listener the traffic is cleartext, with no mediation layer such as a load balancer or WAF in front of the origin instance.

A 0.0.0.0/0 default route through the internet gateway is attached, via aws_route_table.portal_routes, to both subnet associations, making all workloads in those subnets internet-routable with no network segmentation; this route is what turns the open SSH rule into a live attack path.
